attractions.name: Birmingham Botanical Gardens
attractions.description: 67.5 acres of beautiful gardens with over 12,000 different plants.

attractions.name: Birmingham Civil Rights Institute
attractions.description: Museum documenting the Civil Rights Movement in Birmingham.

attractions.name: Vulcan Park and Museum
attractions.description: Home to the world's largest cast-iron statue with panoramic city views.

attractions.name: Birmingham Zoo
attractions.description: Alabama zoo in Mountain Brook home to about 500 animals of 165 species, with seasonal family events.

attractions.name: McWane Science Center
attractions.description: Downtown science center with hands-on exhibits, live science demonstrations, the World of Water aquarium and an IMAX dome theater.

attractions.name: Railroad Park
attractions.description: 19-acre downtown park beside the railroad tracks, with a lake, walking paths, rolling lawns and skyline views.

attractions.name: Oak Mountain State Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 20 km from Birmingham. Alabama's largest state park, with lakes, forested ridges, Peavine Falls and many miles of hiking and biking trails.

attractions.name: Sloss Furnaces National Historic Landmark
attractions.description: Preserved 1880s blast furnace complex that made pig iron until 1971, now a free industrial history museum with guided tours.

attractions.name: Southern Museum of Flight
attractions.description: Aviation museum near Birmingham's airport with military and civil aircraft, including an A-12 Blackbird, and the Alabama Aviation Hall of Fame.

attractions.name: U.S. Space & Rocket Center
attractions.description: Home of the Saturn V moon rocket, Space Camp simulators, and a planetarium — a full-day family favorite.

attractions.name: Huntsville Botanical Garden
attractions.description: 118 acres of themed gardens, a giant open-air butterfly house, and a children's garden built for exploring.

attractions.name: Little River Canyon National Preserve
attractions.description: Day trip · about 95 km from Huntsville. One of the deepest canyons east of the Mississippi, with a scenic rim drive, waterfalls, and family hiking trails.

attractions.name: Cathedral Caverns State Park
attractions.description: Guided 90-minute walk through Cathedral Caverns, featuring a massive cave entrance and large stalagmite formations, including 'Goliath', one of the largest stalagmites in the world, along a paved path.

attractions.name: Monte Sano State Park
attractions.description: Mountaintop state park above Huntsville with scenic overlooks, the North Alabama Japanese Garden, 20 miles of hiking trails and 14 miles of biking trails.

attractions.name: Burritt on the Mountain
attractions.description: Mountaintop museum with a historic park of 19th-century farm houses, barnyard animals, nature trails and views over Huntsville.

attractions.name: EarlyWorks Children's Museum
attractions.description: Hands-on children's history and science museum in downtown Huntsville, part of the EarlyWorks museum complex with Alabama Constitution Village.

attractions.name: USS Alabama Battleship Memorial Park
attractions.description: Historic WWII battleship and military park on Mobile Bay.

attractions.name: Mobile Botanical Gardens
attractions.description: 100-acre botanical garden showcasing Gulf Coast plants and longleaf pine forest.

attractions.name: Mobile Museum of Art
attractions.description: Art museum in Langan Park with a permanent collection of over 6,400 works of American, European, African, and Asian art, including paintings, sculptures, and decorative art.

attractions.name: Gulf Coast Exploreum Science Center
attractions.description: Downtown science center with hands-on exhibit halls, a giant-screen dome theater and touring exhibitions.

attractions.name: Bellingrath Gardens and Home
attractions.description: Day trip · about 30 km from Mobile. 65-acre estate garden on the Fowl River with azaleas, a rose garden, bayou boardwalks and a 1935 house museum.

attractions.name: Colonial Fort Condé
attractions.description: Partial reconstruction of the 1720s French fort that guarded Mobile, with cannons, ramparts and exhibits, run by the History Museum of Mobile.

attractions.name: Fort Gaines
attractions.description: Day trip · about 50 km from Mobile. Well-preserved 19th-century brick fort at the mouth of Mobile Bay, a key site in the 1864 Battle of Mobile Bay.

groceries.name: Publix Super Market at Patchwork Farms
groceries.description: Supermarket. No Jewish community source confirms a kosher section here; packaged items with a hechsher may be stocked, so call ahead before relying on it.

groceries.name: Trader Joe's Birmingham
groceries.description: Supermarket. No Jewish community source confirms a kosher section here; packaged items with a hechsher may be stocked, so call ahead before relying on it.

shuls.name: Knesseth Israel Congregation (Orthodox)
shuls.description: An active, warm Orthodox congregation offering daily minyanim, Shabbat services, and community educational classes.

shuls.name: Temple Beth-El (Conservative)
shuls.description: A historic Conservative synagogue in the Southside neighborhood, serving the Birmingham Jewish community since 1907.

shuls.name: Etz Chayim Synagogue (Conservative)
shuls.address: 7705 Bailey Cove Rd SE, Huntsville, AL 35802
shuls.description: An active Conservative synagogue offering weekly Shabbat services, holiday celebrations, and religious educational programs.

shuls.name: Temple B'nai Sholom (Reform)
shuls.description: The oldest synagogue building in continuous use in Alabama, serving the Reform Jewish community since 1876.

shuls.name: Congregation Ahavas Chesed (Conservative)
shuls.description: A warm, multi-generational Conservative synagogue offering weekly services, youth activities, and adult learning.

shuls.name: Springhill Avenue Temple (Reform)
shuls.description: Alabama's oldest Jewish congregation, founded in 1844, offering meaningful Reform worship and deep community engagement.

hotels.name: Hotel Wildemont, Autograph Collection
hotels.description: Splendid premium boutique hotel situated right next to the Birmingham Botanical Gardens and Lane Park, offering luxurious boutique rooms.

hotels.name: The Redmont Hotel Birmingham, Curio Collection
hotels.description: Highly-rated historic landmark hotel in downtown Birmingham, with a beautiful rooftop lounge and classic Art Deco styling.

hotels.name: The Westin Huntsville
hotels.description: An upscale, lakeside hotel located in Bridge Street Town Centre, offering excellent dining, lake views, and premium spacious suites.

hotels.name: AC Hotel by Marriott Huntsville Downtown
hotels.description: A sleek, modern hotel in the heart of downtown Huntsville, overlooking Big Spring Park and close to top local museums.

hotels.name: The Battle House Renaissance Mobile Hotel & Spa
hotels.description: A historic, landmark luxury hotel with an exquisite vaulted stained-glass ceiling, fine spa, and beautiful historic rooms.

hotels.name: The Admiral Hotel Mobile
hotels.description: A stylishly updated, retro-modern hotel in the historic district, with a great pool and chic mid-century Southern hospitality.

attractions.name: Tony Knowles Coastal Trail
attractions.description: An 11-mile paved multi-use trail along Anchorage's coast, used for walking, running, biking, rollerblading, and in winter cross-country skiing, open 24/7 year-round.

attractions.name: Alaska Native Heritage Center
attractions.description: A renowned cultural center celebrating the traditions, songs, and historical dwellings of Alaska’s Indigenous peoples.

attractions.name: Anchorage Museum
attractions.address: Anchorage Museum, C Street, downtown Anchorage, AK 99501
attractions.description: Alaska's largest museum, covering Alaska Native cultures, history, science and the Arctic, with a hands-on discovery center for kids and a planetarium.
attractions.location: Anchorage Museum, C Street, downtown Anchorage, AK 99501

attractions.name: Alaska Wildlife Conservation Center
attractions.description: Day trip · about 65 km from Anchorage. Drive-through and walking sanctuary for orphaned and injured Alaska animals, including brown and black bears, moose, wood bison, musk oxen and elk.

attractions.name: Flattop Mountain Trail
attractions.address: Glen Alps Trailhead, Chugach State Park, Anchorage, AK
attractions.description: Alaska's most-climbed peak, a steep 3-mile round trip in Chugach State Park from the Glen Alps trailhead to a flat summit with views of Anchorage and Denali.
attractions.location: Glen Alps Trailhead, Chugach State Park, Anchorage, AK

attractions.name: Earthquake Park
attractions.address: Earthquake Park, W Northern Lights Blvd, Anchorage, AK 99517
attractions.description: Coastal park where the 1964 Great Alaska Earthquake slid a neighborhood into the inlet, with interpretive signs, trails through the slide area and views of Denali.
attractions.location: Earthquake Park, W Northern Lights Blvd, Anchorage, AK 99517

attractions.name: Alaska Aviation Museum
attractions.description: Museum on Lake Hood, the world's busiest seaplane base, with restored bush planes, hangars and a viewing area for floatplane takeoffs.

attractions.name: Beluga Point (Turnagain Arm)
attractions.address: Beluga Point Viewpoint, Seward Hwy, Anchorage, AK
attractions.description: Day trip · about 25 km from Anchorage. Rocky pullout on the scenic Seward Highway along Turnagain Arm, known for views of the bore tide, mountains and, in season, beluga whales.
attractions.location: Beluga Point Viewpoint, Seward Hwy, Anchorage, AK

attractions.name: Potter Marsh (Anchorage Coastal Wildlife Refuge)
attractions.address: Potter Marsh boardwalk, Seward Hwy, Anchorage, AK 99516
attractions.description: Boardwalk over a wetland refuge at the south edge of Anchorage for watching nesting waterfowl, bald eagles, salmon and occasionally moose.
attractions.location: Potter Marsh boardwalk, Seward Hwy, Anchorage, AK 99516

attractions.name: Eklutna Lake
attractions.address: Eklutna Lake Rd, Chugach State Park, AK 99577
attractions.description: Day trip · about 45 km from Anchorage. Glacier-fed turquoise lake in Chugach State Park with a lakeside trail for biking and walking, kayaking and mountain views.
attractions.location: Eklutna Lake Rd, Chugach State Park, AK 99577

attractions.name: Mendenhall Glacier Recreation Area
attractions.description: A spectacular 13-mile-long river of ice winding into Mendenhall Lake, featuring the roaring Nugget Falls trail.

attractions.name: Mount Roberts Tramway
attractions.description: Rises 1,800 feet through lush rainforest to mountain-top vistas of the Gastineau Channel.

attractions.name: Tracy Arm Fjord
attractions.description: A narrow, glacier-carved fjord in the Tongass National Forest south of Juneau, within the Tracy Arm-Fords Terror Wilderness, known for waterfalls, floating ice, wildlife, and the Sawyer Glaciers.

attractions.name: Alaska State Museum
attractions.description: State museum of Alaska history, Native cultures and natural history in the modern Andrew P. Kashevaroff building.

attractions.name: Glacier Gardens Rainforest Adventure
attractions.description: Botanical garden in the Tongass rainforest famous for "flower towers," upside-down tree trunks planted with flowers, with guided cart rides up the mountainside.

attractions.name: Macaulay Salmon Hatchery
attractions.description: Working salmon hatchery with a fish ladder where returning salmon climb in late summer, plus aquariums of Southeast Alaska sea life.

attractions.name: Last Chance Mining Museum
attractions.address: Last Chance Mining Museum, Basin Rd, Juneau, AK 99801
attractions.description: Historic compressor building of the Alaska-Juneau gold mine in Gold Creek basin, with original machinery, mining tools and a 3D map of the tunnels.
attractions.location: Last Chance Mining Museum, Basin Rd, Juneau, AK 99801

attractions.name: Perseverance Trail
attractions.address: Perseverance Trailhead, end of Basin Rd, Juneau, AK 99801
attractions.description: Juneau's first road, now a trail up Gold Creek valley past waterfalls, old mine ruins and cool-air mine shafts, starting minutes from downtown.
attractions.location: Perseverance Trailhead, end of Basin Rd, Juneau, AK 99801

attractions.name: Chena Hot Springs
attractions.description: Hot springs resort about 60 miles east of Fairbanks with an outdoor geothermal mineral-water lake (Rock Lake), an indoor pool, Northern Lights viewing, and guided tours of the Aurora Ice Museum.

attractions.name: Alaskaland
attractions.description: A 44-acre historical park in Fairbanks, originally known as Alaskaland and later renamed Pioneer Park. It features museums and exhibits on early Alaskan pioneer life, including a gold rush-era mining display and a preserved Sternwheeler riverboat (the SS Nenana).

attractions.name: University of Alaska Museum of the North
attractions.description: Striking white museum on the UAF campus with Alaska's natural and cultural history, a famous mummified steppe bison and gold collections.

attractions.name: Riverboat Discovery
attractions.description: Three-hour sternwheeler cruise on the Chena and Tanana rivers with a bush-pilot demonstration, sled-dog kennel stop and a re-created Athabascan village.

attractions.name: Creamer's Field Migratory Waterfowl Refuge
attractions.description: Former dairy farm turned refuge in town, with trails and boardwalks where sandhill cranes and geese gather in spring and fall, and a historic farmhouse visitor center.

attractions.name: Kenai Fjords National Park Glacier Cruise
attractions.description: Board a scenic vessel to witness massive calving glaciers crash into the sea and spot wild seals, puffins, and humpbacks.

attractions.name: Exit Glacier Nature Hike
attractions.description: An accessible walking trail that leads right to the edge of a towering, brilliant blue glacial flow.

attractions.name: Alaska SeaLife Center
attractions.description: Public aquarium and marine research center on Resurrection Bay with Steller sea lions, harbor seals, puffins and a touch tank.

attractions.name: Caines Head State Recreation Area
attractions.address: Caines Head SRA, south of Seward on Resurrection Bay (coastal trail from the Lowell Point area, or by boat)
attractions.description: Coastal park south of Seward with beach hikes (timed with low tide) and the WWII Fort McGilvray bunkers on a headland above Resurrection Bay.
attractions.location: Caines Head SRA, south of Seward on Resurrection Bay (coastal trail from the Lowell Point area, or by boat)

attractions.name: Seward Waterfront Park
attractions.description: Mile-long shoreline park and path along Resurrection Bay with mountain views, interpretive signs and frequent sea otter sightings.

attractions.name: Alyeska Aerial Tramway
attractions.description: An aerial tramway at Alyeska Resort that glides up the mountain to an observation deck at 2,300 feet, offering panoramic views of surrounding peaks and glaciers.

attractions.name: Virgin Creek Falls Trail
attractions.description: A short, well-marked trail, about 0.4 to 0.5 mile round trip, through temperate rainforest to a small waterfall and pool near Alyeska Resort in Girdwood.

attractions.name: Crow Creek Gold Mine
attractions.description: Historic 1890s gold mine with original buildings where visitors pan for gold in Crow Creek.

attractions.name: Winner Creek Trail
attractions.address: Winner Creek trailhead near Alyeska Resort, Girdwood, AK 99587
attractions.description: Boardwalk and forest trail through temperate rainforest from Alyeska to Winner Creek Gorge, where the creek rushes through a narrow canyon.
attractions.location: Winner Creek trailhead near Alyeska Resort, Girdwood, AK 99587

attractions.name: Begich, Boggs Visitor Center (Portage Lake)
attractions.address: Begich, Boggs Visitor Center, Portage Lake, Chugach National Forest, AK (mailing: 145 Forest Station Rd, Girdwood)
attractions.description: Forest Service visitor center on Portage Lake with exhibits on glaciers and views of icebergs and Portage Glacier's valley.
attractions.location: Begich, Boggs Visitor Center, Portage Lake, Chugach National Forest, AK (mailing: 145 Forest Station Rd, Girdwood)

attractions.name: Denali Glacier Landing Flightseeing
attractions.address: 229.5 Parks Hwy, Denali National Park and Preserve, AK 99755
attractions.description: Soar past sheer granite faces of Denali and land on a massive active glacier to step onto pristine snow fields.

attractions.name: Talkeetna River Walk
attractions.description: Stroll along gravel bars at the confluence of the Talkeetna, Chulitna, and Susitna Rivers, with panoramic views of Denali and the Alaska Range.

attractions.name: Denali State Park (Byers Lake & K'esugi Ridge)
attractions.address: Byers Lake, Mile 147 Parks Hwy, Denali State Park, AK
attractions.description: Day trip · about 45 km from Talkeetna. Large state park beside the Parks Highway with lake and ridge trails and some of the best roadside views of Denali, at viewpoints like Denali View South (Mile 135.2).
attractions.location: Byers Lake, Mile 147 Parks Hwy, Denali State Park, AK

attractions.name: Savage River Scenic Loop Trail
attractions.address: Denali National Park and Preserve, Park Rd, Alaska 99755
attractions.description: A 2-mile riverside walking loop following the Savage River through a canyon between Mount Margaret and Healy Ridge in Denali National Park and Preserve, featuring subalpine tundra flora.

attractions.name: Denali Park Road Transit Tour
attractions.description: Take the national park transit bus into deep pristine wilderness to search for moose, caribou, grizzly bears, and wolves.

attractions.name: Denali Sled Dog Kennels
attractions.address: Park Headquarters on Denali Park Rd, a short drive/shuttle from Denali Visitor Center, AK 99755
attractions.description: The only sled-dog kennels in a U.S. national park, where rangers' working huskies live; visitors meet the dogs and, in summer, watch sled demonstrations.
attractions.location: Park Headquarters on Denali Park Rd, a short drive/shuttle from Denali Visitor Center, AK 99755

attractions.name: Horseshoe Lake Trail
attractions.address: Horseshoe Lake trailhead near Denali Visitor Center, Denali National Park, AK
attractions.description: Easy 3-mile loop down to an oxbow lake along the Nenana River, a good spot to see beavers and moose near the park entrance.
attractions.location: Horseshoe Lake trailhead near Denali Visitor Center, Denali National Park, AK

attractions.name: Mount Healy Overlook Trail
attractions.address: Trailhead near Denali Visitor Center, Denali National Park, AK
attractions.description: Steep 5-mile round-trip climb from the park entrance area to a ridge overlook of the Nenana River valley and the Alaska Range.
attractions.location: Trailhead near Denali Visitor Center, Denali National Park, AK

attractions.name: The Homer Spit
attractions.description: A narrow 4.5-mile strip of land extending into Kachemak Bay, known for fishing, beachcombing, shops, restaurants and a working boat harbor, with a paved 4-mile walking and biking path.

attractions.name: Kachemak Bay State Park Water Taxi Tour
attractions.description: Take a brief water taxi over pristine waters to explore rugged coastlines, towering glaciers, and mossy pine hiking trails.

attractions.name: Alaska Islands & Ocean Visitor Center
attractions.description: Visitor center of the Alaska Maritime National Wildlife Refuge with seabird-colony exhibits and trails to Bishop's Beach through wetlands.

attractions.name: Pratt Museum
attractions.description: Museum of Kachemak Bay's natural history and people, with marine aquariums, a historic homestead cabin and forest trails.

attractions.name: Bishop's Beach
attractions.description: Wide, driftwood-strewn beach in town facing Kachemak Bay and the glaciated Kenai Mountains, great for tidepooling at low tide.

attractions.name: 26 Glacier High-Speed Marine Cruise
attractions.description: Board an ultra-smooth high-speed catamaran to view twenty-six spectacular active glaciers calving into the deep waters of Prince William Sound.

attractions.name: Portage Pass Glacier Hiking Trail
attractions.description: A scenic 2-mile alpine hike that crosses Portage Pass, offering sweeping views of Portage Glacier and Lake. Suitable for a range of hikers, with a steeper initial climb.

attractions.name: Anton Anderson Memorial Tunnel
attractions.description: North America's longest highway tunnel at 2.5 miles, a one-lane passage shared on a timed schedule by cars and Alaska Railroad trains.

attractions.name: Begich Towers
attractions.description: Former Army barracks where nearly the whole town lives under one 14-story roof, with the post office, police and shops inside; seen from outside, it's a striking piece of Cold War history.

attractions.name: Passage Canal & Whittier Glacier view
attractions.description: Deep fjord at Whittier's harbor framed by hanging glaciers and waterfalls, the starting point for Prince William Sound cruises.

attractions.name: Worthington Glacier State Recreation Site
attractions.description: State recreation site in Thompson Pass, about 28 miles north of Valdez on the Richardson Highway. A short paved, wheelchair-accessible trail leads to a viewing platform overlooking Worthington Glacier, often called one of Alaska's most accessible glaciers. Open until closed by winter snow.

attractions.name: Keystone Canyon Waterfalls
attractions.description: Drive through a breathtakingly narrow sheer canyon flanked by towering waterfalls like Horsetail Falls and Bridal Veil Falls.

attractions.name: Valdez Museum
attractions.description: Museum of Valdez history, from the gold-rush trail and the 1964 earthquake that destroyed the old town to the Trans-Alaska Pipeline terminal, with an 1886 hand-pumped fire engine.

attractions.name: Historic Creek Street Boardwalk
attractions.description: A historic wooden boardwalk built on stilts over Creek Street stream, now home to cozy local art galleries and gift shops.

attractions.name: Misty Fjords National Monument Floatplane Tour
attractions.description: Floatplane flightseeing tours from Ketchikan over Misty Fjords National Monument, with views of granite cliffs rising about 3,000 feet from the fjords, waterfalls and lakes. Tours run about 1-2 hours, and some include a landing stopover.

attractions.name: Deer Mountain Trail
attractions.description: Steep rainforest trail starting near downtown that climbs to alpine views over Ketchikan, the Tongass Narrows and surrounding islands.

attractions.name: White Pass & Yukon Route Railroad
attractions.description: A narrow-gauge vintage rail excursion from Skagway that travels through dramatic mountain scenery, passing canyon gorges, waterfalls, and tunnels along the historic White Pass route.

attractions.name: Klondike Gold Rush National Historical Park
attractions.description: National historical park preserving the history of the 1897-98 Klondike Gold Rush. In Skagway it includes over 20 historic buildings, four of them museums. The visitor center at 2nd Ave and Broadway has old photos, films and ranger talks.

attractions.name: Dyea & Chilkoot Trail trailhead
attractions.address: Dyea, Klondike Gold Rush National Historical Park (via Dyea Rd from Skagway), AK 99840
attractions.description: Site of the vanished 1897 boomtown at the start of the Chilkoot Trail, with tide flats, ruins of the old wharf and the first easy miles of the gold-rush trail.
attractions.location: Dyea, Klondike Gold Rush National Historical Park (via Dyea Rd from Skagway), AK 99840

attractions.name: Yakutania Point & Smuggler's Cove
attractions.address: Yakutania Point trail (across the footbridge from downtown), Skagway, AK 99840
attractions.description: Easy 2-mile loop from town over the Skagway River footbridge to rocky lookouts and a quiet cove on Taiya Inlet.
attractions.location: Yakutania Point trail (across the footbridge from downtown), Skagway, AK 99840

attractions.name: Skagway Museum
attractions.description: Community museum in the 1899 granite McCabe College building, with gold-rush artifacts, Tlingit items and stories of Skagway's boom years.

attractions.name: Sitka National Historical Park Totem Walk
attractions.address: Sitka National Historical Park, 103 Monastery St, Sitka, AK 99835
attractions.description: Stroll scenic loop trails under giant moss-draped spruce trees, decorated with majestic hand-carved Haida and Tlingit totem poles.

attractions.name: Fortress of the Bear
attractions.description: Rescue center for orphaned brown and black bear cubs, housed in former pulp-mill clarifier tanks, with viewing platforms over the habitats.

attractions.name: Castle Hill (Baranof Castle State Historic Site)
attractions.address: Castle Hill, Harbor Way, Sitka, AK 99835
attractions.description: Hilltop site where Alaska was formally transferred from Russia to the United States in 1867, with a short ramp, cannons and views over Sitka Sound.
attractions.location: Castle Hill, Harbor Way, Sitka, AK 99835

chabad.notes: Contact in advance for Shabbat hospitality.

shuls.address: 7525 E Northern Lights Blvd, Anchorage, AK 99504
shuls.description: Reform congregation led by Rabbi Abram Goodstein. Features regular Shabbat services and vibrant community life.

shuls.hours: No published schedule — contact ahead for service times.
shuls.notes: Reform congregation; only synagogue in Southeast Alaska. Contact ahead for service times.

shuls.description: Reform congregation; farthest-north synagogue building in the world.
shuls.hours: Davening times change weekly; check with the shul for current times.
shuls.notes: Reform congregation; northernmost synagogue building in the world. Check with the congregation for service times.

shuls.description: Reform, small congregation serving the Kenai Peninsula. Does not maintain a permanent building and meets in members' homes.
shuls.hours: Contact ahead for meeting schedule and location.
shuls.notes: Reform congregation with no permanent building; meets in members' homes. Contact ahead note required before visiting.

attractions.name: Desert Botanical Garden
attractions.description: 140 acres of desert trails with 50,000 plants, themed gardens, and seasonal events like the butterfly pavilion and holiday luminarias.

attractions.name: Phoenix Zoo
attractions.description: One of the country's largest nonprofit zoos: over 3,000 animals on themed trails, giraffe feeding, a stingray touch tank, and camel rides.

attractions.name: Heard Museum
attractions.description: Internationally renowned museum of American Indian art, from Hopi katsina dolls to contemporary Native works, with family programs and events.

attractions.name: Children's Museum of Phoenix
attractions.description: Hands-on children's museum in the historic Monroe School Building in downtown Phoenix, with more than 300 play experiences across three floors, including a climber, an art studio and a children's garden.

attractions.name: Musical Instrument Museum (MIM)
attractions.description: Museum displaying thousands of musical instruments from about 200 countries, with headphone audio-video guides and a hands-on Experience Gallery.

attractions.name: Arizona Science Center
attractions.description: Hands-on science museum in downtown Phoenix's Heritage and Science Park with interactive galleries and a planetarium.

attractions.name: Papago Park and Hole-in-the-Rock
attractions.description: Desert park of red sandstone buttes on the Phoenix-Tempe border, with the short, kid-friendly Hole-in-the-Rock trail to a natural opening overlooking the city.

attractions.name: South Mountain Park and Preserve
attractions.description: One of the largest city parks in the U.S., with desert hiking trails and a scenic drive to Dobbins Lookout over the Phoenix valley.

attractions.name: Japanese Friendship Garden of Phoenix (Ro Ho En)
attractions.description: Three-and-a-half-acre Japanese stroll garden in central Phoenix with a koi pond, waterfall, stone lanterns and a tea house.

attractions.name: Hall of Flame Museum of Firefighting
attractions.address: 6101 E Van Buren St, Phoenix, AZ 85008
attractions.description: Large firefighting museum with over 130 restored fire engines and equipment from 1725 to modern times, plus a kids' play area.
attractions.location: 6101 E Van Buren St, Phoenix, AZ 85008

attractions.name: Wildlife World Zoo, Aquarium & Safari Park
attractions.address: 16501 W Northern Ave, Litchfield Park, AZ 85340
attractions.description: Day trip · about 35 km from Phoenix. Large West Valley zoo and aquarium with giraffes, rhinos, big cats, a safari train and walk-through aquariums.
attractions.location: 16501 W Northern Ave, Litchfield Park, AZ 85340

attractions.name: Boyce Thompson Arboretum
attractions.description: Day trip · about 85 km from Phoenix. Arizona's oldest and largest botanical garden, with desert plant collections, a lake and trails along Queen Creek below Picketpost Mountain.

attractions.name: Lake Pleasant Regional Park
attractions.address: 41835 N Castle Hot Springs Rd, Morristown, AZ 85342
attractions.description: Day trip · about 55 km from Phoenix. Maricopa County park on a large desert reservoir north of Phoenix with boating, scenic overlooks, trails and a visitor center.
attractions.location: 41835 N Castle Hot Springs Rd, Morristown, AZ 85342

attractions.name: Arizona Railway Museum
attractions.description: Day trip · about 30 km from Phoenix. Volunteer-run outdoor museum in Chandler with historic locomotives and passenger cars from Arizona's railroads.

attractions.name: OdySea Aquarium
attractions.description: The Southwest's largest aquarium: 6,000 animals across 65 exhibits, touch pools, and penguin encounters.

attractions.name: McCormick-Stillman Railroad Park
attractions.address: 7301 E Indian Bend Rd, Scottsdale, AZ 85250
attractions.description: City park with a miniature train ride around the grounds, a 1950s carousel, railroad museum buildings and big playgrounds.
attractions.location: 7301 E Indian Bend Rd, Scottsdale, AZ 85250

attractions.name: McDowell Sonoran Preserve (Gateway Trailhead)
attractions.address: 18333 N Thompson Peak Pkwy, Scottsdale, AZ 85255
attractions.description: Scottsdale's huge protected Sonoran Desert preserve with over 200 miles of trails; the Gateway trailhead has easy loops and routes toward Thompson Peak.
attractions.location: 18333 N Thompson Peak Pkwy, Scottsdale, AZ 85255

attractions.name: Western Spirit: Scottsdale's Museum of the West
attractions.description: Smithsonian-affiliated museum in Old Town Scottsdale on the history and art of the American West, from Native American artifacts to cowboy gear.

attractions.name: Lost Dutchman State Park
attractions.address: 6109 N Apache Trail, Apache Junction, AZ 85119
attractions.description: Day trip · about 40 km from Scottsdale. State park at the foot of the Superstition Mountains with desert hiking trails, wildflowers in spring and views of the rugged peaks.
attractions.location: 6109 N Apache Trail, Apache Junction, AZ 85119

attractions.name: McDowell Mountain Regional Park
attractions.address: 16300 McDowell Mountain Park Dr, Fountain Hills, AZ 85268
attractions.description: Day trip · about 30 km from Scottsdale. Large Maricopa County desert park northeast of Scottsdale with hiking, biking and horse trails and views of the McDowell Mountains and Four Peaks.
attractions.location: 16300 McDowell Mountain Park Dr, Fountain Hills, AZ 85268

attractions.name: Saguaro Lake
attractions.address: Saguaro Lake Marina, 14011 N Bush Hwy, Mesa, AZ 85215
attractions.description: Day trip · about 35 km from Scottsdale. Reservoir on the Salt River in Tonto National Forest surrounded by saguaro-covered canyon walls, with a marina and boat rentals and tours.
attractions.location: Saguaro Lake Marina, 14011 N Bush Hwy, Mesa, AZ 85215

attractions.name: Fountain Park (Fountain Hills Fountain)
attractions.address: 12925 N Saguaro Blvd, Fountain Hills, AZ 85268
attractions.description: Lakeside park in Fountain Hills whose famous fountain shoots a jet of water hundreds of feet high for 15 minutes every hour during the day.
attractions.location: 12925 N Saguaro Blvd, Fountain Hills, AZ 85268

attractions.name: Scottsdale Historical Museum (Little Red Schoolhouse)
attractions.description: Small free history museum in Scottsdale's 1910 red-brick schoolhouse on the Civic Center mall, telling the town's pioneer story.

attractions.name: Usery Mountain Regional Park
attractions.address: 3939 N Usery Pass Rd, Mesa, AZ 85207
attractions.description: Day trip · about 30 km from Scottsdale. Desert park in east Mesa with the Wind Cave trail up Pass Mountain, nature trails and a nature center.
attractions.location: 3939 N Usery Pass Rd, Mesa, AZ 85207

attractions.name: Slide Rock State Park
attractions.description: A natural red-rock waterslide in Oak Creek Canyon, on a historic apple orchard homestead — one of Arizona's most popular spots to cool off in summer.

attractions.name: Bell Rock
attractions.address: Bell Rock Trailhead, 4999 AZ-179, Sedona, AZ 86351
attractions.description: Bell-shaped red sandstone butte beside Highway 179 with an easy pathway around its base and scrambles partway up.
attractions.location: Bell Rock Trailhead, 4999 AZ-179, Sedona, AZ 86351

attractions.name: Airport Mesa Scenic Overlook
attractions.description: Mesa-top overlook in West Sedona with 360-degree views of the red rock formations, especially popular at sunset.

attractions.name: Red Rock State Park
attractions.address: Lower Red Rock Loop Rd, Sedona, AZ 86336
attractions.description: Nature preserve along Oak Creek with easy trails, red-rock views and a visitor center focused on environmental education.
attractions.location: Lower Red Rock Loop Rd, Sedona, AZ 86336

attractions.name: West Fork Trail (Oak Creek Canyon)
attractions.address: Call of the Canyon day-use area, AZ-89A, Oak Creek Canyon, Sedona, AZ 86336
attractions.description: Popular shaded trail up a narrow side canyon of Oak Creek Canyon, crossing the creek between towering red and white cliffs; great in fall colors.
attractions.location: Call of the Canyon day-use area, AZ-89A, Oak Creek Canyon, Sedona, AZ 86336

attractions.name: Crescent Moon Picnic Site (Red Rock Crossing)
attractions.address: End of Red Rock Crossing Rd, Sedona, AZ 86336
attractions.description: Forest Service day-use area on Oak Creek with the classic view of Cathedral Rock reflected in the water, plus creekside paths and picnic areas.
attractions.location: End of Red Rock Crossing Rd, Sedona, AZ 86336

attractions.name: Montezuma Castle National Monument
attractions.address: 2800 Montezuma Castle Hwy, Camp Verde, AZ 86322
attractions.description: Day trip · about 30 km from Sedona. Well-preserved 800-year-old Sinagua cliff dwelling set high in a limestone cliff above Beaver Creek, seen from a short paved loop.
attractions.location: 2800 Montezuma Castle Hwy, Camp Verde, AZ 86322

attractions.name: Out of Africa Wildlife Park
attractions.address: 3505 W State Route 260, Camp Verde, AZ 86322
attractions.description: Day trip · about 30 km from Sedona. Wildlife park in Camp Verde with a safari bus tour among giraffes and zebras, big cats, and animal feeding demonstrations.
attractions.location: 3505 W State Route 260, Camp Verde, AZ 86322

attractions.name: Verde Canyon Railroad
attractions.description: Day trip · about 30 km from Sedona. Scenic excursion train from Clarkdale through the remote Verde River canyon, past red rock cliffs, a tunnel and bald eagle nesting areas.

attractions.name: Lowell Observatory
attractions.description: Where Pluto was discovered: daytime science exhibits and nighttime telescope viewing under some of the darkest skies in the U.S.

attractions.name: Grand Canyon National Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 130 km from Flagstaff. One of the world's great natural wonders: a mile-deep canyon with rim viewpoints, ranger programs, and family trails.

attractions.name: Grand Canyon Railway
attractions.description: A historic train ride (running since 1901) that departs from Williams, Arizona and travels through the high desert to the South Rim of the Grand Canyon, featuring Western-themed musicians and cowboy entertainment on board.

attractions.name: Meteor Crater
attractions.description: The best-preserved meteorite impact site on Earth — nearly a mile wide — with rim trails, a space museum, and a 4D experience.

attractions.name: Walnut Canyon National Monument
attractions.description: Forested canyon east of Flagstaff where the Island Trail passes 25 cliff-dwelling rooms built by the Sinagua people about 800 years ago.

attractions.name: Sunset Crater Volcano National Monument
attractions.description: Young cinder-cone volcano north of Flagstaff with a loop road and trails across black lava flows and cinder fields.

attractions.name: Wupatki National Monument
attractions.address: 25137 N Sunset Crater-Wupatki Loop Rd, Flagstaff, AZ 86004
attractions.description: Day trip · about 45 km from Flagstaff. Red sandstone pueblo ruins of homes built about 900 years ago on the open grasslands north of Flagstaff, on the same loop road as Sunset Crater.
attractions.location: 25137 N Sunset Crater-Wupatki Loop Rd, Flagstaff, AZ 86004

attractions.name: Museum of Northern Arizona
attractions.address: 3101 N Fort Valley Rd, Flagstaff, AZ 86001
attractions.description: Museum of the natural and cultural history of the Colorado Plateau, with geology, dinosaur and Native American art collections.
attractions.location: 3101 N Fort Valley Rd, Flagstaff, AZ 86001

attractions.name: Riordan Mansion State Historic Park
attractions.description: Arts-and-Crafts style log-and-stone duplex mansion built in 1904 for two lumber-baron brothers, shown on guided tours.

attractions.name: Bearizona Wildlife Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 45 km from Flagstaff. Drive-through wildlife park in the pines of Williams where bears, wolves, bison and other North American animals roam, plus a walk-through area.

attractions.name: Horseshoe Bend
attractions.description: A short desert walk to the iconic overlook where the Colorado River loops 270 degrees through 1,000-foot sandstone cliffs.

attractions.name: Antelope Canyon
attractions.description: World-famous slot canyon with swirling sandstone walls and light beams, visited only on guided tours led by Navajo guides.

attractions.name: Monument Valley Navajo Tribal Park
attractions.description: The classic Western-movie landscape of towering red buttes, seen on the 17-mile scenic loop or a Navajo-guided tour.

attractions.name: Glen Canyon Dam and Carl Hayden Visitor Center
attractions.address: US-89 at Glen Canyon Dam, Page, AZ 86040
attractions.description: Visitor center perched beside the 710-foot Glen Canyon Dam with exhibits on its construction and views down into the canyon and across Lake Powell.
attractions.location: US-89 at Glen Canyon Dam, Page, AZ 86040

attractions.name: Lake Powell (Wahweap Marina boat tours)
attractions.description: Vast reservoir of the Colorado River in Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, explored on guided boat tours from Wahweap Marina into its red-rock side canyons.

attractions.name: Navajo Bridge Interpretive Center
attractions.description: Pair of steel arch bridges 470 feet above the Colorado River at Marble Canyon; walk the historic span and watch for California condors.

attractions.name: Toadstool Hoodoos Trail
attractions.address: Toadstool Trailhead, US-89 (about 44.5 miles east of Kanab), Kane County, UT
attractions.description: Day trip · about 45 km from Page. Easy desert hike in Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument to balanced-rock hoodoos with boulder caps on slender sandstone pillars.
attractions.location: Toadstool Trailhead, US-89 (about 44.5 miles east of Kanab), Kane County, UT

attractions.name: Lees Ferry
attractions.address: Lees Ferry Rd, Marble Canyon, AZ 86036
attractions.description: Historic Colorado River crossing at the start of the Grand Canyon, with riverside trails, a pioneer ranch site and towering Vermilion Cliffs.
attractions.location: Lees Ferry Rd, Marble Canyon, AZ 86036

attractions.name: Saguaro National Park
attractions.description: Giant saguaros towering over scenic loop drives and easy desert trails, with both East and West districts family-friendly.

attractions.name: Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum
attractions.description: Part zoo, part botanical garden, part natural-history museum — two miles of trails through live desert habitats.

attractions.name: Pima Air & Space Museum
attractions.description: One of the world's largest aircraft museums: nearly 400 planes across 80 acres, including an SR-71 Blackbird and a B-52.

attractions.name: Kartchner Caverns State Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 75 km from Tucson. Guided tours through a limestone cave with living rock formations, discovered in 1974 and kept secret before opening to the public in 1999.

attractions.name: Sabino Canyon Recreation Area
attractions.address: 5700 N Sabino Canyon Rd, Tucson, AZ 85750
attractions.description: Desert canyon in the Santa Catalina foothills with a narrated tram ride and trails along Sabino Creek among saguaros and cottonwoods.
attractions.location: 5700 N Sabino Canyon Rd, Tucson, AZ 85750

attractions.name: Mount Lemmon Scenic Byway
attractions.address: Windy Point Vista, Catalina Hwy (Sky Island Scenic Byway), Tucson, AZ 85749
attractions.description: Winding mountain road climbing from the Sonoran Desert to pine forest near the 9,159-foot summit of Mount Lemmon, with lookouts like Windy Point.
attractions.location: Windy Point Vista, Catalina Hwy (Sky Island Scenic Byway), Tucson, AZ 85749

attractions.name: Tucson Botanical Gardens
attractions.description: Urban botanical garden with themed desert, cactus, and tropical gardens and a seasonal butterfly exhibit.

attractions.name: Reid Park Zoo
attractions.description: Midsize city zoo in Reid Park with an African savanna, elephants, a South American section and a children's play area.

attractions.name: Biosphere 2
attractions.description: Day trip · about 40 km from Tucson. University of Arizona research facility under giant glass domes, with guided tours through its rainforest, ocean and desert biomes.

attractions.name: Colossal Cave Mountain Park
attractions.address: 16721 E Old Spanish Trail, Vail, AZ 85641
attractions.description: Day trip · about 35 km from Tucson. Mountain park southeast of Tucson with guided tours of a large dry limestone cave, plus a historic ranch and trails.
attractions.location: 16721 E Old Spanish Trail, Vail, AZ 85641

attractions.name: Titan Missile Museum
attractions.address: 1580 W Duval Mine Rd, Sahuarita, AZ 85629
attractions.description: Day trip · about 35 km from Tucson. Cold War Titan II missile silo, the only one preserved for the public, with guided tours down to the launch control center and the missile.
attractions.location: 1580 W Duval Mine Rd, Sahuarita, AZ 85629

attractions.name: Casa Grande Ruins National Monument
attractions.description: Fascinating historic ruins of an ancient Hohokam four-story walled compound dating back to the 14th century, offering guided tours and beautiful desert walks.

attractions.name: Picacho Peak State Park
attractions.address: Picacho Peak State Park, Picacho, AZ 85141
attractions.description: Day trip · about 40 km from Casa Grande. Landmark volcanic peak off I-10 with challenging cable-assisted summit trails, easier desert loops, spring wildflowers and the site of Arizona's largest Civil War battle.
attractions.location: Picacho Peak State Park, Picacho, AZ 85141

attractions.name: Rooster Cogburn Ostrich Ranch
attractions.description: Day trip · about 45 km from Casa Grande. Quirky roadside ranch where visitors hand-feed ostriches, deer, goats, ducks, stingrays and lorikeets.

attractions.name: Casa Grande Mountain Park
attractions.address: 2766 S Isom Rd, Casa Grande, AZ 85122
attractions.description: City desert park with hiking and mountain-bike trails up Casa Grande Mountain, overlooking the valley toward Picacho Peak.
attractions.location: 2766 S Isom Rd, Casa Grande, AZ 85122

attractions.description: 33-acre zoo in War Memorial Park with over 400 animals, a train, an antique carousel and a playground. A $12 million expansion began in 2025, adding new habitats. The zoo stays open during construction.

attractions.description: Day-use park with hiking trails up Pinnacle Mountain and a new visitor center.

attractions.name: Little Rock Central High School National Historic Site
attractions.description: Visitor center and guided tours honoring the Little Rock Nine and school desegregation.

attractions.name: Hot Springs National Park

attractions.name: Wings Over the Rockies Air & Space Museum

attractions.name: Georgia Aquarium
attractions.description: The largest aquarium in the U.S., home to whale sharks, beluga whales, manta rays, and dolphin and sea lion presentations — a full-day family must-see.

attractions.name: Zoo Atlanta
attractions.description: Founded in 1889 in Grant Park, Zoo Atlanta is one of the oldest zoos in the U.S. It is a 40-acre zoo with over 1,000 animals from 200+ species, including giant pandas, elephants, and one of North America's largest populations of western lowland gorillas.

attractions.name: World of Coca-Cola
attractions.description: Interactive museum tracing Coca-Cola's history in Atlanta, with a 4-D theater, the Vault of the Secret Formula, and a tasting room where visitors can sample beverages from around the world.

attractions.name: Martin Luther King Jr. National Historical Park
attractions.description: Free NPS historical park featuring Dr. King's birth home, visitor-center exhibits ('Courage To Lead'), and The King Center along historic Auburn Avenue.

attractions.name: Fernbank Museum of Natural History
attractions.description: Dinosaurs, a giant-screen theater, and 75 acres of old-growth forest trails and outdoor WildWoods exhibits — Atlanta's science and nature experience.

attractions.name: Tellus Science Museum
attractions.description: Day trip · about 65 km from Atlanta. Smithsonian-affiliate science museum in Cartersville, about 45 minutes north of downtown Atlanta, with geology and fossil displays, the Bentley Planetarium, an observatory, and Fossil Dig and Gem Panning areas.

attractions.name: Amicalola Falls State Park & Lodge
attractions.description: Day trip · about 90 km from Atlanta. A Georgia state park and lodge near Dawsonville featuring Amicalola Falls, hiking trails, mountain views, a restaurant, zip-lining, and activities like archery and hatchet throwing.

attractions.name: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park
attractions.description: Preserves a 2,965-acre Civil War battleground of the 1864 Atlanta Campaign. The visitor center has a short film, a museum and artifacts, and the top of Kennesaw Mountain offers views of downtown Atlanta.

attractions.name: Ocmulgee Mounds National Historical Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 120 km from Atlanta. Ancient Native American earthworks with a museum of 12,000 years of history, a reconstructed Earth Lodge, and eight miles of trails — free to enter.

attractions.name: Stone Mountain Park
attractions.description: 3,200-acre park around the world's largest exposed granite, with a skyride to the summit, scenic railroad, family attractions, and the famous laser light show.

attractions.name: Roosevelt's Little White House State Historic Site
attractions.description: Day trip · about 100 km from Atlanta. FDR's preserved personal retreat, kept as he left it, with a museum featuring the Unfinished Portrait and his hand-controlled 1938 Ford convertible.

attractions.name: Atlanta Botanical Garden
attractions.description: 30-acre garden beside Piedmont Park with a tropical conservatory, an orchid house and the Kendeda Canopy Walk through the treetops.

attractions.name: Center for Puppetry Arts
attractions.description: Puppetry museum and theater in Midtown with live puppet shows for children, a Jim Henson collection and hands-on puppet workshops.

attractions.address: 1978 Island Ford Pkwy, Sandy Springs, GA 30350

attractions.location: 1978 Island Ford Pkwy, Sandy Springs, GA 30350

attractions.name: Children's Museum of Atlanta
attractions.address: 275 Centennial Olympic Park Dr NW, Atlanta, GA 30313

attractions.name: The Breman Museum (William Breman Jewish Heritage Museum)

attractions.name: Delta Flight Museum

attractions.name: Chattahoochee Nature Center
attractions.description: Day trip · about 30 km from Atlanta. 127-acre nature center in Roswell with river boardwalks through wetlands, woodland trails and rescued birds of prey.

attractions.name: Panola Mountain State Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 25 km from Atlanta. Protected granite monadnock east of Atlanta with rare rock-outcrop plants, nature trails, ranger-led mountain hikes and a treetop adventure course.

attractions.name: Sweetwater Creek State Park
attractions.address: 1750 Mount Vernon Rd, Lithia Springs, GA 30122
attractions.description: Day trip · about 25 km from Atlanta. State park west of Atlanta where a creek-side trail leads to the brick ruins of the New Manchester textile mill, burned in the Civil War.
attractions.location: 1750 Mount Vernon Rd, Lithia Springs, GA 30122

attractions.name: Jimmy Carter Presidential Library and Museum
attractions.description: Presidential museum of Jimmy Carter's life and term, with a full-scale Oval Office replica and Japanese-style gardens.

attractions.name: Callaway Gardens

attractions.name: Forsyth Park
attractions.description: Savannah's 30-acre historic park, featuring the 1858 cast-iron fountain, basketball and tennis courts, walking paths, and open green space.

attractions.name: Old Fort Jackson

attractions.name: Lincoln Park Zoo

attractions.name: Garfield Park Conservatory

attractions.name: Millennium Park
attractions.description: Free downtown lakefront park with the famous Cloud Gate ("The Bean"), interactive Crown Fountain, and summer family concerts.

attractions.name: The Morton Arboretum

attractions.name: Naper Settlement

attractions.name: Starved Rock State Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 130 km from Chicago. Illinois' most-visited state park, on the Illinois River near Oglesby, with 18 sandstone canyons, seasonal waterfalls, 13 miles of trails, and a lodge. Offers hiking, fishing and boating.

attractions.name: Anderson Japanese Gardens

attractions.name: Skydeck Chicago

attractions.name: 360 CHICAGO Observation Deck

attractions.name: Navy Pier

attractions.name: Lincoln Park Conservatory
attractions.description: Victorian glasshouse from the 1890s in Lincoln Park with palm, fern and orchid rooms; free entry with a timed reservation.

attractions.name: Chicago History Museum
attractions.description: Museum of Chicago's story, from the Great Fire of 1871 to the city's neighborhoods, with historic objects, a vintage L car and hands-on galleries.

attractions.name: Brookfield Zoo Chicago

attractions.name: Chicago Children's Museum

attractions.name: Kohl Children's Museum

attractions.name: Six Flags Great America

attractions.name: Chicago Botanic Garden
attractions.description: 385-acre garden on islands in a chain of lakes, with 27 display gardens including a Japanese garden, a model railroad garden and lakeside trails.

attractions.name: Grosse Point Lighthouse
attractions.description: 1873 lighthouse on the Evanston lakefront, a National Historic Landmark, with seasonal tower tours and a maritime museum in the keepers' quarters.

attractions.name: The Grove National Historic Landmark
attractions.description: 135-acre nature preserve with trails, an interpretive center with live animals and the restored 1856 Kennicott family home.

attractions.name: Ryerson Woods (Edward L. Ryerson Conservation Area)

attractions.name: The Children's Museum of Indianapolis

attractions.name: Eagle Creek Park
attractions.description: One of the largest city parks in the US, with a reservoir, ornithology center, nature trails and boat rentals.

attractions.name: Indiana Statehouse
attractions.description: Limestone state capitol completed in 1888 with a stained-glass rotunda dome; free guided tours on weekdays.

attractions.name: Studebaker National Museum
attractions.description: Three floors of gleaming Studebakers, vintage carriages, and the carriage Lincoln rode to Ford's Theatre.

attractions.name: Fort Wayne Zoo
attractions.description: Day trip · about 110 km from South Bend. AZA-accredited zoo in Fort Wayne with over 1,000 animals, giraffe feedings, and a red panda exhibit (Red Panda Ridge).

attractions.name: Indiana Dunes National Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 65 km from South Bend. 15 miles of Lake Michigan beaches, towering sand dunes, and 50 miles of trails through dunes, wetlands, and prairies.

attractions.name: Shipshewana Trading Place Auction & Flea Market
attractions.description: Billed as the Midwest's largest flea market, this outdoor market in Shipshewana is the size of 30 football fields. Open Tue & Wed, May–Sept, 8am–4pm. Antique, livestock and horse auctions run weekly year-round. Free admission; parking $5.

attractions.name: Lincoln Boyhood National Memorial
attractions.description: Day trip · about 120 km from Bloomington. Walk the pioneer farm where Abraham Lincoln grew from age 7 to 21, with a working living-history farm and visitor center.

attractions.name: Holiday World & Splashin' Safari
attractions.description: Day trip · about 120 km from Bloomington. Family-owned theme and water park with top-ranked wooden coasters, world-record water slides, and free parking, drinks, and sunscreen.

attractions.description: Day trip · about 100 km from Bloomington. Rugged limestone canyon carved by Clifty Creek near Madison, overlooking the Ohio River, with several waterfalls, a fossil-filled creek bed, hiking trails, a campground, a nature center and the Clifty Inn.

attractions.name: McCormick's Creek State Park
attractions.address: 250 McCormicks Creek Park Rd, Spencer, IN 47460
attractions.description: Indiana's first state park, with a limestone canyon, waterfalls on McCormick's Creek and wooded hiking trails.
attractions.location: 250 McCormicks Creek Park Rd, Spencer, IN 47460

attractions.description: Theme park in Altoona, Iowa, near Des Moines, with over 100 rides including coasters like Tornado, plus the Adventure Bay water park.

attractions.description: Iowa State University's 17-acre public garden in Ames, featuring an indoor conservatory, a butterfly wing, and over 20 themed garden areas; named a Top 10 North American garden worth traveling for in 2023.

attractions.description: Heritage railroad running steam and diesel excursion trains through the Des Moines River Valley, crossing a high trestle bridge over Bass Point Creek. Operated by the Iowa Railroad Historical Society in Boone, Iowa.

attractions.description: 500-acre outdoor museum walking through 300 years of Iowa: an Ioway Indian village, pioneer farm, frontier town, and 1900 horse-powered farm.

attractions.name: Covered Bridges of Madison County
attractions.description: Six historic covered bridges on a free, self-guided scenic byway through rolling Madison County farmland, open year-round with no admission fee; you can walk through most of them.

attractions.name: Gray's Lake Park

attractions.description: A 1,200+ acre working horse farm with live horse shows, horse-drawn trolley tours, the International Museum of the Horse, horseback/pony rides, and a campground.

attractions.name: Mary Todd Lincoln House
attractions.description: The girlhood home of Mary Todd Lincoln, wife of President Abraham Lincoln, now a museum with period furniture, family portraits and original Todd and Lincoln family artifacts. Self-guided and guided tours are offered.

attractions.name: Cumberland Falls State Resort Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 130 km from Lexington. Home of the "Niagara of the South," a 68-foot waterfall and one of the few places on earth where you can see a moonbow.

attractions.name: Newport Aquarium
attractions.description: Day trip · about 120 km from Lexington. Aquarium in Newport, Kentucky, across the river from downtown Cincinnati, with sharks, penguins, rays, a jellyfish room and walk-through tunnels, plus Shark Bridge, a suspended rope bridge just inches above a tank of sharks.

attractions.name: Natural Bridge State Resort Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 75 km from Lexington. A 78-foot sandstone arch with a skylift ride, family trails, and the surrounding Daniel Boone National Forest.

attractions.name: Red River Gorge
attractions.description: Day trip · about 80 km from Lexington. A dramatic canyon of natural arches and sandstone cliffs with easy family trails, scenic overlooks, and the historic Nada Tunnel.

attractions.name: Big Bone Lick State Historic Site
attractions.description: Day trip · about 95 km from Lexington. The "birthplace of American paleontology," where mammoths and mastodons once roamed — features a museum with fossil exhibits, salt springs, and hiking trails.

attractions.name: Raven Run Nature Sanctuary
attractions.description: Nature sanctuary in the inner Bluegrass with ten miles of trails through meadows, woodlands and streams, and remnants of early 19th-century settlers' homes.

attractions.name: McConnell Springs
attractions.description: 26-acre park around the springs where Lexington was named in 1775, with trails past blue holes, sinks and a spring run.

attractions.name: Aviation Museum of Kentucky
attractions.description: Aviation museum at Blue Grass Airport with restored military and civil aircraft and the Kentucky Aviation Hall of Fame.

groceries.name: Kroger
groceries.description: Supermarket. No Jewish community source confirms a kosher section here; packaged items with a hechsher may be stocked, so call ahead before relying on it.

attractions.name: Audubon Zoo

attractions.name: Audubon Aquarium & Insectarium
attractions.description: Riverfront aquarium showcasing Gulf of Mexico marine life, with the Insectarium's butterflies and giant bugs in the same complex.

attractions.name: Mardi Gras World
attractions.description: Guided daytime tours through the working float studios of Kern Studios, where artists and craftsmen build New Orleans' Mardi Gras parade floats.

attractions.name: The National WWII Museum
attractions.description: A major New Orleans museum with immersive galleries, interactive experiences including a submarine exhibit and 4-D theater, suited for visitors of all ages.

attractions.name: Fontainebleau State Park
attractions.description: 2,800 acres on Lake Pontchartrain with 1829 sugar-mill ruins, the Tammany Trace bike trail, a sandy beach, and nature trails.

attractions.name: New Orleans City Park
attractions.description: 1,300-acre park with century-old live oaks, lagoons, a miniature train, the Carousel Gardens amusement park and Storyland playground.

attractions.name: New Orleans Botanical Garden
attractions.description: 10-acre garden inside City Park with more than 2,000 plant varieties, a conservatory, a Japanese garden and a model train garden.

attractions.name: Louisiana Children's Museum
attractions.address: 15 Henry Thomas Dr, New Orleans, LA 70124
attractions.description: Children's museum on 8.5 acres in City Park with indoor exhibits on the Mississippi River and food, plus outdoor wetland and garden play areas.
attractions.location: 15 Henry Thomas Dr, New Orleans, LA 70124

attractions.name: Audubon Park
attractions.description: 350-acre Uptown park with lagoons, huge live oaks, a 1.8-mile path, playgrounds and a bird rookery on Ochsner Island.

attractions.name: New Orleans Pharmacy Museum
attractions.description: Museum in an 1823 French Quarter apothecary shop, showing the history of pharmacy and medicine with antique bottles, instruments and a courtyard garden.

attractions.name: Honey Island Swamp Tours (Dr. Wagner's)
attractions.description: Day trip · about 50 km from New Orleans. Narrated boat tours into the Honey Island Swamp, a protected Pearl River wilderness of cypress, bayous, alligators and wading birds.

attractions.name: Louisiana's Old State Capitol
attractions.description: Castle-like Gothic Revival former capitol, now a free museum of Louisiana political history.

attractions.name: Baton Rouge Zoo
attractions.description: AZA-accredited zoo with tigers, giraffes, rhinos, and alligators, plus a train ride, playground, and hands-on KidsZoo.

attractions.name: Jungle Gardens

attractions.name: Vermilionville

attractions.name: Portland Head Light and Fort Williams Park

attractions.description: Maritime museum on a 20-acre campus on the Kennebec River in Bath, on the site of the historic Percy & Small Shipyard. attractions.name: Coastal Maine Botanical Gardens

attractions.name: Wolfe's Neck Woods State Park

attractions.name: Reid State Park

attractions.name: Maine Wildlife Park
attractions.description: Wildlife park in Gray, about 25 minutes from Portland, run by Maine Inland Fisheries & Wildlife. It houses over 30 native Maine species that were injured, orphaned or human-dependent, such as bobcats, foxes, porcupines and raptors. It also has nature trails, picnic areas and daily keeper talks.

attractions.name: Pemaquid Point Lighthouse Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 65 km from Portland. Dramatic wave-washed rocks around an 1827 lighthouse, with a fishermen's museum, learning center, and art gallery.

attractions.name: Marginal Way

attractions.description: 1807 maritime signal tower on Munjoy Hill, the last of its kind in the US. Seasonal guided climbs to the top for harbor views.

attractions.name: Maine Narrow Gauge Railroad Museum
attractions.description: Two-foot-gauge train rides along Casco Bay on the Eastern Prom, with a museum of the old Maine narrow-gauge cars. The railroad plans a future move to Gray.

attractions.name: Two Lights State Park
attractions.description: Cape Elizabeth headland park with rocky ledges, tide pools and WWII bunkers, beside the two Cape Elizabeth lighthouses.

attractions.name: Scarborough Marsh Audubon Center
attractions.description: Maine's largest salt marsh, about 3,100 acres. Maine Audubon runs a nature center there, with marsh trails and seasonal canoe and kayak rentals.

attractions.name: Camden Hills State Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 70 km from Bar Harbor. Hiking trails and an auto road to the Mount Battie summit for sweeping Penobscot Bay views, plus a seaside campground.

attractions.name: Owls Head Transportation Museum
attractions.description: Day trip · about 80 km from Bar Harbor. An operating collection of pre-1940 aircraft, antique cars, motorcycles, bicycles and engines, with interactive exhibits, outdoor demonstrations and seasonal events including family programs. Open year-round.

attractions.name: Fort Knox State Historic Site and Penobscot Narrows Observatory
attractions.description: A 19th-century granite fort paired with a 420-foot bridge observatory offering 360-degree views of the Penobscot River and Bay.

attractions.name: Farnsworth Art Museum
attractions.description: Day trip · about 80 km from Bar Harbor. A celebrated collection of American and Maine art, including the Wyeth Center, with family-friendly programming.

attractions.name: Rockland Breakwater Lighthouse
attractions.description: Day trip · about 75 km from Bar Harbor. A 7/8-mile granite breakwater walk in Rockland, Maine, ending at an 1902 lighthouse with seasonal volunteer-led tours and a keeper's house to explore.

attractions.name: Asticou Azalea Garden
attractions.description: Japanese-inspired garden in Northeast Harbor (1956) with azaleas, rhododendrons, a pond and a raked sand garden. Seasonal.

attractions.name: Bar Harbor Shore Path
attractions.description: Free walking path of about a mile along Frenchman Bay from the town pier, past old summer cottages and rocky shore.

attractions.description: Museum of Jewish life in Maryland that includes the 1845 Lloyd Street Synagogue, the third-oldest standing synagogue building in the US.

attractions.description: Day trip · about 150 km from Moab. National park in south-central Utah along the Waterpocket Fold, a monocline nearly 100 miles long with colorful rock layers, cliffs, canyons and domes. Pioneer-era orchards at historic Fruita allow picking ripe fruit in season where signs are posted.

attractions.name: Corona Arch Trail
attractions.address: Corona Arch Trailhead, Potash Rd (UT-279), Moab, UT 84532
attractions.description: Popular 3-mile round-trip hike outside the national parks to a massive 140-foot sandstone arch, with views of the Colorado River canyon.
attractions.location: Corona Arch Trailhead, Potash Rd (UT-279), Moab, UT 84532

attractions.name: Mill Canyon Dinosaur Trail
attractions.address: Mill Canyon Rd, off US-191 (about 15 miles north of Moab), UT
attractions.description: Short interpretive trail with real dinosaur fossils left in place, plus a nearby boardwalk over one of the most diverse dinosaur trackways in North America.
attractions.location: Mill Canyon Rd, off US-191 (about 15 miles north of Moab), UT

attractions.name: Fisher Towers
attractions.address: Fisher Towers Trailhead, Fisher Towers Rd off UT-128, Moab, UT 84532
attractions.description: Day trip · about 25 km from Moab. Towering dark-red mudstone spires up to 900 feet tall along the Colorado River, explored on a dramatic canyon trail.
attractions.location: Fisher Towers Trailhead, Fisher Towers Rd off UT-128, Moab, UT 84532

attractions.name: Upper Colorado River Scenic Byway (UT-128)
attractions.address: UT-128 at the Colorado River bridge (Lions Park), north of Moab, UT 84532
attractions.description: The "River Road," a 44-mile drive along the Colorado River through red-rock canyons with views of Castle Valley and Fisher Towers.
attractions.location: UT-128 at the Colorado River bridge (Lions Park), north of Moab, UT 84532

attractions.name: Moab Museum
attractions.description: Small regional museum on Moab's geology, dinosaurs, uranium mining and pioneer history.

attractions.name: Zion Canyon & Angels Landing
attractions.description: Gigantic soaring sandstone cliffs, river narrows, and majestic trails.

attractions.name: Bryce Canyon National Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 80 km from Zion National Park. A forest of red-rock hoodoos with easy rim viewpoints and family trails like Queen's Garden, plus world-class stargazing.
attractions.location: Day trip from Zion National Park

attractions.name: Cedar Breaks National Monument
attractions.description: A 2,500-foot-deep amphitheater of multicolored cliffs and spires at 10,000 feet, with short family trails and dark-sky programs.

attractions.name: Best Friends Animal Sanctuary
attractions.description: The nation's largest no-kill animal sanctuary, in Angel Canyon near Kanab. It is home to up to 1,600 dogs, cats, horses, pigs and other animals, and offers free daily tours, hiking trails and a café.

attractions.name: Zion National Park
attractions.description: Towering red cliffs, the Virgin River, and family-friendly trails like the Riverside Walk, served by a free shuttle system.

attractions.name: Snow Canyon State Park
attractions.description: Red-and-white sandstone canyon with lava tubes, petrified dunes, and short kid-friendly hikes minutes from town.

attractions.name: Kolob Canyons (Zion National Park)
attractions.address: Kolob Canyons Visitor Center, Kolob Canyons Rd, New Harmony, UT 84757
attractions.description: Quieter northwest district of Zion off I-15, with a 5-mile scenic drive among red finger canyons, viewpoints and trails away from the main-canyon crowds.
attractions.location: Kolob Canyons Visitor Center, Kolob Canyons Rd, New Harmony, UT 84757

attractions.name: Canyon Overlook Trail
attractions.address: Trailhead at east entrance of Zion-Mount Carmel Tunnel, UT-9, Zion National Park, UT
attractions.description: Short, rewarding 1-mile round-trip trail on Zion's east side ending at a cliff-top view straight down lower Zion Canyon.
attractions.location: Trailhead at east entrance of Zion-Mount Carmel Tunnel, UT-9, Zion National Park, UT

attractions.name: Coral Pink Sand Dunes State Park
attractions.address: Coral Pink Sand Dunes State Park, Kane County (near Kanab), UT
attractions.description: Day trip · about 40 km from Zion National Park. State park of shifting coral-colored sand dunes below vermilion cliffs, with sandboard and sled rentals and a dune boardwalk.
attractions.location: Coral Pink Sand Dunes State Park, Kane County (near Kanab), UT

attractions.name: St. George Dinosaur Discovery Site at Johnson Farm
attractions.address: 2180 E Riverside Dr, St. George, UT 84790
attractions.description: Day trip · about 50 km from Zion National Park. Museum built over a major dinosaur trackway discovered in 2000, with hundreds of preserved Early Jurassic footprints and fossils.
attractions.location: 2180 E Riverside Dr, St. George, UT 84790

attractions.name: Sand Hollow State Park
attractions.address: Sand Hollow State Park, Hurricane, UT 84737
attractions.description: Day trip · about 35 km from Zion National Park. Warm blue reservoir framed by red sandstone near Hurricane, popular for boating, paddleboarding and dune-buggy riding on its sand mountain.
attractions.location: Sand Hollow State Park, Hurricane, UT 84737

attractions.name: Pioneer Park (St. George)
attractions.description: Day trip · about 55 km from Zion National Park. Free 52-acre city park of red sandstone with slot-like crevices, bouldering and Dixie Rock, overlooking St. George.

groceries.description: Carries kosher dry goods, grape juice, challah, and frozen kosher items serving Zion visitors.

attractions.name: Burlington Waterfront Park Walk
attractions.description: Beautiful lakeside views of the Adirondack peaks.

attractions.name: ECHO, Leahy Center for Lake Champlain
attractions.description: Waterfront science center and aquarium with hands-on exhibits, live animals, and the ecology and history of Lake Champlain.

attractions.name: Church Street Marketplace
attractions.description: Four-block open-air pedestrian mall in Burlington with 100+ shops and restaurants, live entertainment, and year-round events.

attractions.name: Hildene, The Lincoln Family Home
attractions.description: Day trip · about 150 km from Burlington. Robert Todd Lincoln's Georgian mansion with formal gardens, a restored Pullman railcar, and a working goat dairy farm on a 412-acre estate in Manchester, Vermont.

attractions.name: Shelburne Museum
attractions.description: Museum of American art, design and history on a 45-acre campus with 39 buildings, 25 of them historic and relocated to the site. Collections include folk art, quilts, decoys and carriages, plus a carousel, the Round Barn and the 220-foot steamboat Ticonderoga.

attractions.name: Shelburne Farms
attractions.description: 1,400-acre working farm and National Historic Landmark with a children's farmyard, cheesemaking, and walking trails on Lake Champlain.

attractions.name: Vermont Teddy Bear Factory
attractions.description: Factory tours showing how handcrafted teddy bears are made, plus the Bear "hospital" and a gift shop beloved by kids.

attractions.name: Lake Champlain Maritime Museum
attractions.description: Lakeside campus with shipwreck exhibits, a replica 1776 gunboat, a working boat shop, and hands-on sailing programs for kids.

attractions.name: Lake Placid Olympic Center
attractions.description: Home of the 1932 and 1980 Winter Olympics, with the Lake Placid Olympic Museum, public ice skating sessions, and historic arenas including the Herb Brooks Arena to visit.

attractions.name: Island Line Trail & Causeway
attractions.description: 14-mile lakeside path from Burlington north along Lake Champlain. It includes the Colchester Causeway, a gravel path running miles out into the lake, with a seasonal bike ferry across the gap.

attractions.name: Ethan Allen Homestead
attractions.description: 1787 farmhouse of Revolutionary War hero Ethan Allen, with a small museum and walking trails along the Winooski River.

attractions.name: Lake Champlain Ferry (Burlington–Port Kent)
attractions.description: Seasonal car-and-passenger ferry from Burlington's waterfront across Lake Champlain to Port Kent, New York, about an hour each way with Adirondack views.

attractions.name: Mount Philo State Park
attractions.description: Vermont's first state park, opened in 1924. A short road or trail climbs to a summit with wide views over Lake Champlain and the Adirondacks.

attractions.name: Red Rocks Park
attractions.description: Lakeside park of about 100 acres in South Burlington, with pine-forest trails along red-rock cliffs over Lake Champlain.

attractions.name: Green Mountain Stowe Recreation Path
attractions.description: The Stowe Recreation Path is a free, 5.3-mile paved public path running from Stowe Village to Topnotch Resort on the Mountain Road. It follows the West Branch Little River, crosses it on several bridges, and is used for walking, running and biking.

attractions.name: Vermont State House
attractions.description: The nation's smallest state capital's crown jewel, a Greek Revival capitol with a gold-leaf dome offering free guided tours.

attractions.name: Montshire Museum of Science
attractions.description: Day trip · about 90 km from Stowe. Hands-on science museum in Norwich, VT with 150+ interactive exhibits, an outdoor water-play area, and miles of nature trails.

attractions.name: Quechee State Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 95 km from Stowe. Home to Quechee Gorge, Vermont's deepest gorge, with the Ottauquechee River 165 feet below. The Quechee Gorge Trail leads to the gorge, a bridge gives views over it, and the river offers trout fishing. The park has a campground and picnic areas.

attractions.name: VINS Nature Center
attractions.description: Day trip · about 95 km from Stowe. 47-acre nature center with 17 raptor enclosures, live bird-of-prey exhibits, and a forest canopy walk.

attractions.name: Fairbanks Museum & Planetarium
attractions.description: Victorian-era natural science museum packed with wildlife displays and fossils, plus Vermont's only public planetarium.

attractions.name: Smugglers' Notch State Park
attractions.description: Dramatic narrow mountain pass with towering cliffs, caves, and family-friendly hiking trails near Stowe; includes a campground and is seasonal (third weekend in May through second Monday in October).

attractions.name: Trapp Family Lodge
attractions.description: Austrian-style mountain resort on 2,600 acres in Stowe, with trails and four seasons of activities, including sleigh rides and snow-covered trail hiking in winter.

attractions.name: Ben & Jerry's Factory Tour
attractions.description: The iconic ice cream factory with guided production tours, an included ice cream sample, and the whimsical Flavor Graveyard.

attractions.name: Cold Hollow Cider Mill
attractions.description: Family-owned cider mill pressing apples the old-fashioned way since 1974, famous for its legendary cider donuts and bakery.

attractions.name: Billings Farm & Museum
attractions.description: Day trip · about 95 km from Stowe. Fully operating Jersey dairy farm and museum of rural life where kids can meet cows, sheep, and draft horses.

attractions.name: Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller National Historical Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 95 km from Stowe. The only national historical park in Vermont, telling the story of American conservation history and land stewardship. Offers guided mansion tours and 25+ miles of carriage roads and trails in the Mount Tom Forest.

attractions.name: Moss Glen Falls
attractions.description: Tall cascade in a narrow gorge in C.C. Putnam State Forest, a short walk from the road just north of Stowe village.

attractions.name: Bingham Falls
attractions.description: Series of falls and deep pools in a gorge off Route 108, reached by a short, steep trail.

attractions.name: Mt. Mansfield Auto Toll Road
attractions.description: Gravel road of about 4.5 miles up to the ridge of Mount Mansfield, Vermont's highest peak, with short walks to alpine views. Summer and fall only.

groceries.name: Price Chopper
groceries.description: Supermarket. No Jewish community source confirms a kosher section here; packaged items with a hechsher may be stocked, so call ahead before relying on it.

groceries.name: Hannaford Supermarket
groceries.description: Supermarket. No Jewish community source confirms a kosher section here; packaged items with a hechsher may be stocked, so call ahead before relying on it.

attractions.name: Virginia Museum of Fine Arts
attractions.description: World-class art with free general admission, open 365 days a year.

attractions.name: George Washington's Mount Vernon
